g.text: ASTRONOMY.
HISTORY.
The number of the planets known to
the ancients was five, besides the
earth. In 1781 Sir William Herschel
discovered the planet Uranus, the
first addition to the system since
the remotest antiquity.
In the first years of the present
century the small planets Ceres,
Pallas, Juno, and Vesta were found
between the orbits of Mars and
Jupiter, and their number has since
been greatly increased.
Lastly, in 1846, the planet Neptune
was found in the place assigned to it
by the calculations of M. Le Verrier
and Mr Adams — the most signal
triumph of physical astronomy.
